subtopic: Quantization granularity / Per-tensor vs per-channel vs per-group
learningObjective: Distinguish per-tensor, per-channel, and per-group quantization by scale/zero-point count and hardware/kernel implications.
stem: For quantizing an FP16 weight matrix `W` of shape `[out_channels, in_channels]` to INT8/INT4 for a subsequent quantized GEMM, which of the following statements about quantization granularity are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Per-tensor uses one (scale, zero-point) pair for the entire W; simplest to implement and cheapest in metadata storage but loses accuracy when different channels have very different value ranges.

Per-channel (also called per-output-channel or per-row here) uses one (scale, zero-point) per row of W; the GEMM epilogue applies a different scale to each output element, adding negligible extra work per output.

Per-group divides the `in_channels` axis into groups (e.g., 128 elements per group) and stores one scale per (row, group) pair; standard for W4A16 kernels where groups of 128 give a good accuracy/memory-metadata trade-off.
Per-tensor is strictly more accurate than per-channel because a single scale allows Tensor Cores to run at peak throughput without any metadata handling.
Per-group quantization is illegal in INT8 GEMM because the accumulator cannot mix multiple scales within one dot product.

explanation: A, B, C are standard characterizations: per-tensor (single scale, low metadata, worst fit on heterogeneous channels), per-channel (one scale per output row, negligible extra epilogue cost), per-group (finer scales along the K axis, the standard for W4A16 GPTQ/AWQ kernels typically with group_size 128). D is false: per-tensor is generally LESS accurate than per-channel because it forces one scale to cover all channels. E is false: per-group INT/W4 GEMMs handle multiple scales along the K axis by partial-accumulating within a group, applying the group scale, then adding to the outer accumulator.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: per-channel implementation and epilogue cost.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: per-group is standard for W4A16.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: per-tensor is generally LESS accurate.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: per-group GEMM handles multiple scales via grouped accumulation.

assumptions: The GEMM kernel is designed for the chosen granularity.
The 'in_channels' axis in this discussion corresponds to the K axis of the matmul.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-group is always better than per-channel — smaller group sizes increase metadata and can offset accuracy gains.
Does not imply per-channel weight quantization always requires per-channel activation quantization; the two are chosen independently.

performanceClaim.scope: Granularity trade-off for quantized weight GEMMs
